To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-terminal domain of LysRS is a functional RNA-binding domain that synergistically increases the affinity of LysRS for tRNA and its efficiency in the aminoacyl-tRNA synthesis reaction.
the extra N-domain of L. tRNALys binding to LysRS and that the extra N-terminal domain of eukaryotic LysRS increases its catalytic efficiency for tRNA aminoacylation.
a novel tRNA-binding domain appended to the catalytic domain of mammalian LysRS provides LysRS, in addition to its amino acid specificity, with the capacity to specifically aminoacylate tRNALys.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying tRNA channeling in mammalian cells.
the elucidation of the structure-function relationship of LysRS from human cells, which is the first step in the design of new antiviral agents.
the molecular basis of tRNA recognition by LysRS and the role of LysRS in the regulation of the expression of HIV-1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-terminal domain of eukaryotic LysRS is a functional tRNA-binding domain.
the extra domain is an RNA-binding domain, but that it is not a specific tRNA binding domain, and therefore it does not play an essential role in the tRNA3 LYS aminoacylation reaction.

the N-domain of LRS is a novel tRNA binding domain that provides the enzyme with the ability to bind tRNA3 LYS and that this domain acts synergistically with the classical catalytic domain to increase the efficiency of tRNA3Lys aminoacylation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LysRS is a two-domain protein that binds tRNA through a synergistic interaction between its catalytic domain and its N-domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-terminal domain of mammalian LysRS is a functional tRNA-binding domain.
the tRNA-binding domain of mammalian LysRS has been co-opted from an ancestral RNA-binding protein and is not a typical tRNA-binding domain.
the N-domain of mammalian LysRS is a bona fide tRNA-binding domain that is essential to the catalytic activity of the enzyme.
